name: trending-repo-digest
description: Turn a trending-projects listing into a plain-English digest: read the page, pull the items out, say why each one is worth your attention given what you have already seen, and file it as one growing record. The host must be on your egress allow-list first.

listing_url.help: The listing page to read — a trending page, a release feed, a front page. Its host must already be listed under Settings → Security → Allowed Egress Hosts, because automated fetches use an EXCLUSIVE allow-list and an unlisted host is refused before any request leaves the machine.

subject.help: What this listing is about, in your words — "trending Python repositories", "new Rust crates". It is the digest's identity, so successive runs update one record rather than filling the store with near-duplicates.

max_picks.help: Ceiling on how many items reach the digest. A digest of thirty entries is a listing again; six is what a person actually reads.

max_chars.help: How much of the listing page to read. This can only NARROW the fetch provider's 20,000-character ceiling — a bigger number gets you the ceiling, never more.

metadata.why_two_extraction_calls: Extraction and framing are different jobs: "what is on this page" is mechanical and belongs on the fast tier, while "why should this person care, given what they already saw" needs the prior digest in context. One prompt asked to do both does both worse, and the cheap half then pays reasoning-tier prices.
metadata.egress_is_the_consent_surface: `net-fetch` reaches nothing until this listing's host sits in `security.egress.allow_hosts`. With an empty list the first run FAILS by design, naming the host and the exact setting — that refusal is how the user grants the reach, and this template has no way to widen it.
metadata.why_it_reports_on_a_quiet_cycle: Unlike market-monitor this one always writes and always delivers, even when nothing is new. "Nothing new since last time", from a watcher you can see, is different information from silence you cannot tell apart from a refused fetch or a dead trigger.

steering_examples.description: Read the trending page and give me the three projects that are actually new to me, with a sentence each on why they matter.
You keep picking up the same three long-running projects — treat anything already in the record as seen and only pitch what is genuinely new.

example_outputs: one digest naming the picks worth a look, each with where it was spotted and why it matters — stored and searchable
metadata.when_not_to_use: not for a single page you want read in full — use dual-sink-watcher; and not for a paper or article, which is paper-ingest
